title: Replace a derailleur chain
summary: Release the old chain, preserve correct routing through the derailleur and verify the replacement chain before riding.

tools.name: Chain tool
tools.note: Needed when sizing or breaking a non-reusable link.

steps.title: Record the chain routing
steps.instruction: Before disconnecting anything, trace the chain around the chainring, cassette and both derailleur pulleys.
steps.why: Incorrect routing through the derailleur cage is a common installation mistake.
steps.check: You can identify the chain path through both derailleur pulleys.

steps.title: Open the chain
steps.instruction: Shift to low chain tension, locate the quick link or chosen break point, then disconnect the chain with the correct tool.
steps.why: Controlled disconnection prevents damage and makes the old chain easy to compare with the replacement.
steps.warning: Use the link type and reuse policy specified by the chain manufacturer.

steps.title: Route the replacement correctly
steps.instruction: Feed the replacement chain around the chainring, cassette and derailleur pulleys following the routing you recorded.
steps.why: The chain must pass on the correct side of derailleur cage tabs and around both pulleys.
steps.warning: A chain routed outside a cage guide can appear connected but will run incorrectly.

steps.title: Verify connection and shifting
steps.instruction: Join the chain using the correct connector, rotate the crank by hand and check that the chain runs freely through every pulley and selected gear.
steps.why: A final low-load inspection can reveal routing or connection errors before they become dangerous under pedaling load.
steps.check: Chain runs smoothly with no tight link, snag or incorrect cage routing.
